name: Lindy
positioning: Lindy presents itself today as a shared AI teammate for email, meetings, Slack and business tools, billed per seat with usage credits.

pricing.model: Per-user monthly subscription with a pool of usage credits (about $0.01 per credit); no per-minute voice pricing found.
pricing.headline: Team plan from $49.99 per user per month for 5,000 credits; $50 free credits for 7 days; no per-minute phone-call rate published on the pages read.
planNotes: Pricing page: Free ($50 in credits, last 7 days), Team from $49.99/month for 5,000 credits (larger credit bundles up to $9,999.50/month), Enterprise custom.
Docs pricing page names plans Plus, Pro and Max and says credits cost $0.01 on base plans; the public pricing page names the paid plan Team. Naming differs between the two pages.
Top-ups at $10 per 1,000 credits; unused monthly credits do not roll over.
Enterprise adds HIPAA with signed BAA, SSO and SCIM, audit logs.
No page read described a phone-call (inbound or outbound voice agent) product or per-minute price, so no per-minute number is recorded.
pricing.freeTrial: $50 in free credits, no credit card required; free credits last 7 days.
whatIsExtra: Each active user in the workspace is billed as a seat

strengths.claim: Connects to 1,500+ integrations and supports MCP servers, per the pricing page.
Approval step is built in: actions with outside impact such as sending an email wait for user approval.
States SOC 2 Type II and GDPR compliance, with HIPAA and a signed BAA on Enterprise.
Lets users choose the model per task and pools credits across the team.

limitations.claim: Monthly credits refresh each cycle and do not roll over; credit-using actions pause when the pool runs out.
Setup docs describe the phone connection as a way to message Lindy by iMessage, SMS or voice notes, not as a line that places or answers calls for a business.

compliance.note: Stated by vendor, self-attested: security doc says SOC 2 Type II, GDPR, HIPAA and PIPEDA; HIPAA with a signed BAA is listed under Enterprise only.

telephony.providedNumbers: Docs mention an assigned Lindy phone number and email address for the assistant, used for texting; no phone-call numbers for business callers were found.

stepsToLeave: Docs describe a versioned memory and skills file system that users can view, edit and share; an explicit export procedure for agents was not found.
The docs site offers a full-docs export for LLMs, which is documentation rather than customer data.

bestFor: Individuals and teams that want a general-purpose AI assistant working across email, calendar, meetings and Slack, rather than a dedicated phone-agent platform.

sources.title: Lindy sitemap (lists blog posts about AI voice agents)

unknowns: Whether Lindy currently sells an AI phone-agent product that answers or places calls for businesses; the home page, pricing page and docs read describe an AI teammate, though the home page role menu lists 'Calls & bookings' and the sitemap still has voice-agent blog posts.
Any per-minute pricing for phone calls.
Whether the 'Calls & bookings' role page exists (the guessed URL returned 404).
